Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 12. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 12 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 3; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters 'XX'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn and poll input, servicing transformation request $30CC through $3393. At four remaining bombs, change the moving trigger to colour 7. Zero bombs completes normally. After death, bullet count $3014=5 identifies the second stage and branches directly to completion regardless of remaining bombs; otherwise check reserves and respawn or exhaust. Cleanup JSR is patched at $30A3. Controlled live comparison: after native transformation with bombs4/request1, holdingLEFT produces a normal death then reaches$5B00 with bombs4; same input in stage1 reaches respawn$3050. No position/death-state edits. Entry through earlier campaign levels remains open. A complete native input replay from the initialized selected level collects nine bombs with one lost life, then reaches trigger contact alive with three remaining. After the transformation, LEFT collects a500-point bomb and dies. At $3078 and completion $5B00, score1400, remaining2, reserves4. No game-state or code edits follow the initialized setup; earlier campaign entry remains unverified.

With an active player collision, bomb count below 5 plus any sprite-7 collision increments request $30CC and returns safely. Otherwise start death mode 1 if the current mode is 0. The main loop consumes transformation requests. Native ordinary-input contact at $30BD has player260,216 and trigger7 actor state252,216, collision shadows$81 for those two only, remaining3 and life0. The original increment requests transformation; source conditions are not supplied by memory edits.
Counter incremented by sprite-7 contact once fewer than five bombs remain. The main loop tests it; transformation routine $3393 decrements it once.

Eight four-byte records [duration,X-low delta,X-high delta,Y delta], followed by $FF to restart. First duration is 19, X delta -4, Y delta 0. The route also alternates vertical +/-2 and horizontal +4 segments. State $3360/$3361 selects the current segment.
One packed 30-byte ladder-like trigger frame, expanded to VIC frame $10 on the first movement callback. Its colour changes from 2 to 7 when four bombs remain.

Once per loaded overlay, initialize sprite 7 at X=208,Y=136 using frame $32BF and route $329E. During active play outside mode 2, add signed X/Y deltas, decrement $3360, and advance to the next four-byte path record at zero. $FF restarts record 0. Initialization selects frame $10, colour 2 and enables the sprite.
Initialized flag $335F, movement duration $3360, and path delta offset $3361, initially 1. The offset points to X-low delta immediately after a record duration.
SID transformation stream: envelope $00/$A0, fifteen frequency/duration records, zero terminator. Routine $3393 queues it with priority 6, release 0, control $10 (triangle).

Install collision callback $34C7, freeze the player movement divider at 9, queue sound $3362, hide the old trigger and load marker sprite $342F through $346E. Temporarily install frame callback $3418, clear the bitmap and draw layout $31AA. Redraw the HUD, copy alignment arrays $3290/$3298, set bullet count 5 and bomb-table pointer $3226, install marker callback $3499, then restore the divider from $402A. Remaining bomb count $3013 is not reset. Controlled live request1/bombs4 executes this full routine, retains4 targets and installs bullet limit5. Subsequent normal input death reaches completion. Controlled original execution checks the pending callback writes, resident $428D installation, frame sequence49/50/51/52, and post-wait replacement layout/ladder fields/table. The CPU check splits before and after the asynchronous wait; native transformation was checked separately. An ordinary-input replay also reaches this entry with remaining3 after nine pickups and one lost life. Returning to $305B keeps remaining3, life0 and score900 while changing bullet limit3 to5. Subsequent death follows the level completion path.
Temporary IRQ callback copies $342E to player frame $407B and cycles frames $31,$32,$33,$34, wrapping before $35. Foreground transformation replaces it with $3499 when finished.
Current player frame $31-$34 for the temporary transformation animation.
63 authored sprite bytes for the 500-point marker. The following copy loop reads 64 bytes, so its own first opcode $A2 at $346E becomes the unused padding byte of the sprite slot.
Copy 64 bytes from $342F to $8400 with X=0..63. The final source byte overlaps this routine; VIC sprite display uses only the first 63 bytes.

Callback for four records in the second bomb table. Add 400 ($0190) to the 24-bit total score, then start marker timer $3498=122. The resident collector subsequently adds its ordinary 100, for 500 total, and decrements the remaining bomb count.
122-update marker duration loaded by the special-bomb callback. Nonzero keeps the popup active; the transition to zero disables its sprite.

At initial count 122, place sprite 7 at player X and player Y-12 (CLC then SBC #11) and increment its enable byte. Each call increments colour and decrements the timer; reaching zero decrements the enable byte. Frame $10 was loaded by $346E.
After transformation, active player collision starts death unless sprite 7 also has any collision, exempting the 500-point marker. Sets mode 1 without checking the previous mode.
